3.label: The player skipped a free or decisive capture (often of the queen, but also rooks, knights, or a promoting pawn), with the specific piece, square, and tactic varying board to board.

8.label: Player overlooks an available capture (usually of an undefended/hanging piece) and plays a non-capturing move instead; the captured piece, square, and tactic vary board to board.

5.label: Self-inflicted blunders where a developed/moved piece (queen, knight, or bishop) lands on an attacked, undefended square and is lost for little or nothing; the specific piece, square, and resulting tactic vary board to board.

0.label: Player overlooks a stronger capturing move (frequently a queen-winning capture like Bxd8/Bxd3/Nxd8) and plays a non-capturing or weaker move instead, with the piece, square, and exact tactic varying board to board.

14.label: The player skips a free/winning capture (the best move grabs an undefended or hanging piece); the captured piece, square, and resulting tactic vary board to board.

6.label: Capturing/trading material prematurely—most often exchanging queens or grabbing a piece—instead of keeping the attacker for mate or a winning line; the piece traded and the missed continuation vary board to board.

9.label: Failing to capture a dangerous attacking piece (most often capturing an invading knight on g6/g3 with the h-pawn), with the specific piece, square, and pawn varying board to board.

13.label: Missed capture — the side to move declines a free/hanging piece (often the blockader of a passed pawn) instead of grabbing it with king or pawn, with the captured piece, square, and capturing unit varying board to board.

11.label: Voluntarily exchanging pieces (usually rooks or queens) into a lost pawn endgame; the piece traded and exact endgame vary, but the self-inflicted trade into a worse position is constant.

4.label: Player gives a check that achieves nothing—losing tempo or hanging material to the recapture—instead of the simple capturing/defending move; the piece checked, the square, and the material dropped vary board to board.

15.label: Player initiates an unfavorable capture/trade that loses material or squanders advantage; the captured piece, recapturing unit, and resulting damage (hung piece, opened file, lost bishop pair, delayed castling) vary board to board.

17.label: Player skips a free or winning capture of an undefended/hanging piece; the captured piece, square, and exact tactic vary board to board, but the constant is an available capture left unplayed.

21.label: The player ignores or mishandles an attacked piece (usually a knight or bishop hit by a pawn), leaving it to be captured for inadequate compensation; the specific piece, square, and attacking unit vary board to board.

22.label: Missed capture — the best move grabs a free enemy piece or pawn (queen, rook, bishop, or pawn) while the player instead makes a non-capturing move, the captured target varying board to board.

7.label: Missed capture — failing to play the available capture of an undefended or decisive piece, where the captured piece (rook, bishop, queen, pawn) and square vary across boards while the failure to take what's free stays constant.

1.label: Playing a slow/passive king or pawn move that squanders a critical tempo instead of the urgent break, capture, or move-order — the lost-time move varies (a-pawn push, king shuffle, prophylactic pawn) but each forfeits the initiative or timing the position demanded.

20.label: The played move squanders time — relocating a piece passively or failing to hit the enemy queen — instead of the tempo-gaining move that attacks the queen and forces a retreat; the piece moved, square, and target queen vary board to board.

10.label: Self-inflicted bad exchange/capture that liquidates the player's own key (often only active or defensive) piece into a lost position or mate; the piece swapped and the resulting endgame vary board to board.

24.label: A passive or careless move that self-inflicts material loss — varying across boards by which unit hangs (pawn, knight, bishop) and which tactic (fork, capture, pawn break) the opponent uses to win it.

26.label: Missed capture — the player declines the best-move capture (most often a simplifying trade/exchange into a won king-and-pawn endgame), with the piece captured, the square, and the follow-up varying board to board.

25.label: Player skipped a forcing capture—usually a queen or rook exchange that resolves the tension first—choosing a non-capturing move instead; the captured piece, square, and resulting tactic vary board to board.

29.label: The player skipped a free or winning capture (queen, rook, knight, or capture-mate) in favor of a non-capturing move; the captured piece, square, and follow-up tactic vary board to board.

31.label: Missed capture — the best move is a capture (of a bishop, knight, pawn, or queen on varying squares, often a thematic exchange or tactical strike) that the player skipped in favor of a non-capturing move.

12.label: Self-inflicted material loss: the player moves a piece to a square where it (or the material it was guarding) gets captured — the piece, square, and resulting tactic vary board to board.

27.label: King safety — the played move weakens or neglects the player's own king (removing a defender, walking into a check/fork, or ignoring the attack), allowing a devastating attack or mate; the exposed king, attacking piece, and missed defensive resource (often a queen trade or prophylactic king move) vary board to board.

2.label: A self-inflicted, non-developing pawn move (wing or center advance) that wastes tempo, loosens the king, or allows the opponent a tactic — the specific pawn, square, and resulting weakness vary board to board.

37.label: Missed capture — the best move is a free or winning capture (queen, rook, knight, etc.) that the player skipped in favor of a check, retreat, or wrong move, varying by piece and square across boards.

34.label: Player skips a favorable capture (most often resolving central tension like ...exd4 or ...exd5/cxd5, but the captured piece and square vary board to board).

30.label: Player makes an unsound capture/sacrifice (most often a bishop grabbing a pawn on h3/h6/g6) that loses material with no compensation — the sacrificed piece, target pawn, and square vary, but it's always self-inflicted material loss for too little.

16.label: A self-inflicted move that places the player's own king or piece on a vulnerable square (often the a7-g1 diagonal), inviting a pin, fork, or skewer that wins material — varying across king walks, queen self-traps, and greedy captures that expose the position.

35.label: The player skipped a winning capture (often an intermediate move/zwischenzug exploiting mutual threats), but the captured piece, square, and exact tactic vary board to board, and a few cases are non-capture queen-trades or checks.

18.label: In king-and-pawn / minor-piece endgames the player walks the king (or shuffles a piece) to the wrong square, abandoning a critical pawn or controlling square; what varies is which square is vacated and which pawn or mating net is given up.

32.label: Self-inflicted pawn advance that prematurely breaks a locked/defensive structure or wastes a needed tempo; the pawn, square, and side vary, and some medium boards substitute a misplaced piece move.

42.label: Self-inflicted hanging of material — the played move leaves a piece (most often the queen, sometimes a rook or bishop) on a square where it can be freely captured; the piece, square, and surrounding tactic vary board to board.

40.label: The player skipped a best-move capture (usually a queen/knight/rook capture defusing the attack) in favor of an irrelevant or passive move; the captured piece, square, and follow-up tactic vary board to board.

33.label: The move played leaves the player's own material exposed to capture or trapping (often a bishop pushed to a bad square instead of a safe retreat, or a move allowing a trap/fork); the specific piece and mechanism vary board to board.

43.label: Player overlooks a free winning capture (rook, queen, or other piece varies board to board), playing a quiet king or pawn move instead of grabbing the hanging material.

28.label: Player throws away a winning attack or forced mate—often by grabbing material or playing a passive/defensive move—instead of continuing the decisive blow; the winning resource abandoned and the distracting move vary board to board.

36.label: The played move abandons the blockade or loses the promotion race, allowing an enemy passed pawn to queen; the pawn's file, promotion square, and the correct stopping method (blockade, king walk, fork-with-check) vary board to board.

38.label: Self-inflicted material loss from premature or unsound sacrifices and forced combinations — the player throws a piece into a check/fork/attack that the opponent simply refutes by capturing, varying by which piece is sacrificed (knight, rook) and which tactic (fork, check, exchange) is botched.

23.label: A forcing checkmate (or decisive forcing win) was available, but the player chose a slow, non-forcing quiet move instead; the specific forcing move—usually a check—and the mate length vary board to board.

48.label: Unsound sacrifice giving up the player's own material for insufficient compensation — the sacrificed piece and target square vary (Bxf7+, Nxf2, etc.) but each move throws away material without follow-up.

49.label: Develops or moves a piece (usually a bishop to g4/g5, but also rooks, knights, pawns) onto an undefended square where it is simply captured—often after an intermezzo check—the piece and square varying board to board.

51.label: Player declines an available capture—often of an undefended queen, rook, or attacker—choosing a passive king/pawn/piece move instead; the captured piece and resulting tactic vary board to board.

47.label: Player overlooks a forced checkmate (mate-in-1 to mate-in-several) and plays an unrelated or greedy move instead; the exact mating piece, square, and depth vary board to board, with a few cases being missed decisive tactics rather than pure mates.

50.label: A self-inflicted material blunder where the played move parks or trades a piece into immediate loss; varies from clear hung bishops in the openings to broader self-inflicted material/king-safety concessions in the typical boards.

53.label: Self-inflicted material loss — the player moves a piece onto an attacked/undefended square or trades a key defender, with the specific piece, square, and whether it's a clean hang or a losing trade varying board to board.

41.label: Squandering the position by playing a slow, non-forcing move instead of the demanded forcing shot — the wasted tactic varies (missed capture, check, zwischenzug, or avoiding a bad trade) but the constant is choosing a passive move that throws away the advantage.

39.label: The player moves their own king to an inferior square—walking it into checks/mate or steering it the wrong way in king-and-pawn endgames—where the specific threat, file, and target square vary board to board.

59.label: Self-inflicted move (often capturing the lone defender or ignoring a threat) that walks the player's own king into checkmate; varies in the mating piece, square, and exact tactic, with a few boards merely collapsing into a lost position rather than forced mate.

52.label: Player makes a passive or off-point move that neglects the position's one decisive threat — usually an enemy passed pawn about to promote, but sometimes an incoming mate or a capture of an undefended piece — and the specific threat ignored varies board to board.

57.label: A piece (usually the queen) deserts a critical defensive post — a guarded square, pawn, or the king's shelter — to make an attacking/repositioning sortie, self-inflicting loss of material; the deserted duty and the piece that falls vary board to board.

61.label: Failing to execute a forced checkmate—usually mate-in-one but ranging up to mate-in-several—by playing a routine capture, check, or king move instead; the mating piece, square, and depth vary board to board.

54.label: The player passes up a winning tactical shot — overwhelmingly a knight fork (often with check) that wins the queen or an exchange — playing a slow/quiet move instead; the forking piece, target, and square vary, and a minority of boards swap the fork for an analogous missed check, capture, or mate.

58.label: Self-inflicted material loss — the move played throws away the player's own material (often by a greedy or unsafe capture/advance), with the specific piece, square, and tactic varying board to board.

56.label: Premature trade — the player grabs/exchanges a piece (most often a bishop capture, also knight or pawn) instead of a stronger waiting or tactical move, dissolving their own advantage; the piece traded, square, and missed resource vary from board to board.

60.label: The played move self-inflicts (accelerates or permits) checkmate of the player's own king — by walking the king into a net, removing a key defender, or skipping the only saving check — and the exact mating mechanism varies across boards.

63.label: Squanders a winning advantage by playing a slow king/piece move instead of the urgent pawn push or breakthrough — the wasted-tempo move and the missed critical push vary board to board.

45.label: Self-inflicted queen mishandling — the player moves the queen onto a square that forces/allows an unfavorable exchange (or abandons a piece) and collapses the position; the trade square, lost endgame, and occasionally the hung piece vary board to board.

62.label: Failing to play a winning queen check that exploits a stuck/uncastled king to win loose material (Qa5+/Qa4+/Qh4+/Qh5+); the exact check square and the piece won vary, with a minority of boards being other missed wins (endgame king moves, missed captures).

55.label: The player moves a piece to an inferior/passive square (or wrong piece/tempo-wasting push), abandoning the strong square and squandering the win — the piece, square, and lost tactic vary, but the self-inflicted relocation that throws away material or advantage is constant.

44.label: Self-inflicted king-exposure blunders — the player moves the king to a bad square or removes a defender, walking into a decisive attack (discovered check, back-rank, or mate) that costs the queen or the game; the exposed piece and exact tactic vary, but the safe alternative is almost always a quiet king/blocking move.

19.label: Self-inflicted: with a winning promotion on the board the player plays a non-promoting move (a check, king step, rook shuffle, or pawn push to the wrong square) instead of queening — the pawn, square, and substitute move vary, and the fuzzier (medium) cases instead step a key piece off its defensive duty.
